Profile the result of a SQL query

Source: R/profile.R
profile_query.Rd

Summarises the rows of a query as a csdb_profile, under disclosure control. Every statistic comes from an aggregate query, and the profile keeps no count below k.

Usage

profile_query(
  connection,
  sql,
  columns = NULL,
  field_types = NULL,
  keys = NULL,
  k = 5L,
  noise = NULL,
  max_levels = 50L,
  group_sizes = NULL,
  crosstabs = NULL,
  dependencies = NULL,
  source = NULL
)

Arguments

connection

A DBI connection, or a DBConnection_v9. For a DBConnection_v9 the function uses $autoconnection.

sql

The query to profile, as one string. The function runs it as the subquery SELECT ... FROM (<sql>) q. The query is published with the profile as provenance$query, so a caller MUST NOT put an identifier literal, such as a person number, in it.

columns

A named character vector or named list that gives the sensitivity of each column: "full", "coarsen", "schema_only" or "exclude". A column that columns does not name is "schema_only".

field_types

A named character vector of csdb field types: TEXT, INTEGER, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, DATE or DATETIME. With NULL, the function infers the types from the R classes of a zero-row fetch.

keys

A character vector of key column names, or NULL.

k

The smallest count that the profile can hold.

noise

NULL, or list(epsilon = e). With epsilon, the function adds Laplace noise of scale 1 / e to each cell count and to each count of missing values. It adds the noise before suppression, then rounds each count and floors it at 0. Call set.seed() first for a reproducible profile.

max_levels

The largest number of distinct values for which a full column publishes its values.

group_sizes

A named list, for example list(rows_per_id = "Id"). Each element names one column. The profile holds how many values of that column have each row count.

crosstabs

A list of pairs of column names, for example list(c("sex", "age_group")). Both columns MUST be "full".

dependencies

A list of pairs of column names. For each pair the profile holds whether the first column determines the second.

source

A label for the data source, or NULL. The profile publishes it.

Value

A list of class csdb_profile, with the elements provenance, field_types, keys, n_rows, columns, group_sizes, crosstabs, dependencies and notes. provenance holds format, source, query, driver, profiled_at (UTC, ISO 8601), k, noise, max_levels and csdb_version. driver is the class of the DBI connection.

Details

Each column of field_types gets a summary from its sensitivity:

  • schema_only: type, sensitivity and missing_share. All other summaries hold these three fields too. An INTEGER or DOUBLE column also holds nonnegative, which is TRUE when its SQL minimum is at least 0.

  • exclude: no entry in columns. The column is in field_types only.

  • full TEXT or BOOLEAN, at most max_levels distinct values: levels and n.

  • full INTEGER, DOUBLE or DATETIME, at most max_levels distinct values: levels and n when every level holds at least k rows. Otherwise the column takes the summary that it has above max_levels. An INTEGER or DOUBLE column with one distinct value always publishes levels. When that value holds fewer than k rows, the function removes its cell, so levels and n are empty.

  • full TEXT, above max_levels: n_distinct, rounded down to a multiple of k.

  • full DATE: counts per day, as days and n.

  • full DATETIME: levels and n, as above, otherwise counts per UTC day as days and n. The function truncates each level to the whole second.

  • coarsen DATE or DATETIME: counts per ISO week, as weeks and n. The Monday of each week is its key. A DATETIME falls in the week of its UTC day.

  • INTEGER and DOUBLE, full above max_levels or coarsen: breaks and n, for the bins [breaks[i], breaks[i + 1]). The breaks are always double.

  • coarsen TEXT or BOOLEAN: an error that names the column.

The breaks come from pretty(c(min, max), n = 20). An end break that equals the observed minimum or maximum moves one step outward. The function removes an inner break that equals either extreme. So no break equals an observed extreme.

Suppression keeps every published count at k or above. On an ordered dimension, a cell below k merges with its neighbours:

  • Days merge into ISO weeks, then calendar months, then calendar quarters. Weeks merge into months, then quarters. The column takes the finest of these resolutions at which every cell holds k. The field name gives the resolution: days, weeks, months or quarters. Each key is the first day of its cell. A week merges into the month of its Monday.

  • When a quarter holds fewer than k rows, adjacent quarters merge into runs. Each run takes quarters in order until it holds k. A last run below k joins the run before it. quarters then holds the first quarter of each run and quarters_to the last.

  • Bins merge into runs in the same way. A merged bin keeps the outer breaks of its run, so no break is added.

  • Group sizes merge into runs in the same way. Each run is published as size_from, size_to and n, the number of values with a row count in that range. The ranges tile the row counts from 1 up with no gap. The first range starts at 1. Every other size_from is an observed row count, the smallest in its run. Each size_to is one below the next size_from. The last range has no size_to, so it runs from its size_from up.

  • A first run that holds only the smallest row count merges with the next run. A last run that holds only the largest merges with the run before it. So no exact smallest or largest row count is published.

A table whose present values number fewer than k publishes no cell. Unordered cells, which are the levels of a TEXT or BOOLEAN column and the cells of a crosstab, do not merge. Each cell below k is removed. A column sums its removed counts into suppressed_n, and it keeps suppressed_n only when that sum is at least k. With noise, the function adds the noise to the finest cells, before it merges or removes any cell.

missing_share is "suppressed" when the count of missing values, or the count of values present, is from 1 to k - 1. n_rows holds no noise. A query with fewer than k rows is an error.

The function reads the data with several queries. It runs them in one read snapshot where the driver gives one:

  • SQLite: one read transaction.

  • PostgreSQL: a transaction at REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY.

  • SQL Server: a transaction at SNAPSHOT when the database allows it, otherwise at REPEATABLE READ. REPEATABLE READ does not stop the rows that other sessions insert. The function puts back the isolation level of the session after the profile.

  • Other drivers, or a connection on which DBI::dbBegin() fails, for example because a transaction is open: no snapshot, and a message says so.

The function sends only SELECT and transaction-control statements, and ends the transaction with a rollback.

The function always refuses a torn profile, with or without a snapshot. The check covers each column with levels, days, weeks, months, quarters or breaks. Its counts before noise and suppression, plus its count of missing values, MUST equal n_rows. For a group-size column, the row counts of its values plus its missing count MUST equal n_rows. Otherwise the function stops with an error that names the column and both totals. A crosstab and an n_distinct have no total to check.

A crosstab counts the rows where both columns hold a value. Each of its columns MUST have levels or be a DATE. A group-size range is a range of row counts, so it can be below k. Only n must reach k. A dependency holds when each value of the first column, NULL included, goes with one value of the second. The profile stores no mapping.

See also

Other profile functions: profile_data(), profile_table(), read_profile(), write_profile()

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:", extended_types = TRUE)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "visits", data.frame(
  id = rep(1:20, each = 3),
  sex = rep(c("female", "male"), 30),
  age = rep(c(4, 15, 38, 52, 71, 90), 10)
))
p <- profile_query(
  con,
  "SELECT * FROM visits",
  columns = c(sex = "full", age = "coarsen", id = "exclude"),
  group_sizes = list(rows_per_id = "id")
)
p$columns$sex
#> $type
#> [1] "TEXT"
#> 
#> $sensitivity
#> [1] "full"
#> 
#> $missing_share
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $levels
#> [1] "female" "male"  
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 30 30
#> 
p$columns$age$breaks
#> [1]  0  5 20 40 55 75 95
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
